markdown.markdown:
Four products: **Radar Gun Live**, **Velocity Heartbeat**, **Effective
Velocity**, and **Late Life**.

::: {.callout-warning}

Spin is not in the SMT data and cannot be recovered from positional tracking
alone. Rather than invent it, this component uses three things that *are*
directly measurable: **release extension**, **movement** (with gravity removed),
and **perceived velocity**.
:::

## Fitting a pitch

Each pitch has 10–12 tracked frames between release (y ≈ 55 ft) and the plate.
We fit **quadratics** to $x(y)$ and $z(y)$ — exactly right, because under
constant acceleration position is quadratic in flight distance. Fitting lets us
evaluate the pitch at *any* distance, which is what tunneling requires.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-fit
#| eval: false
traj <- fit_pitch_trajectory(get_ball_track(gs, play), t_pitch)
traj$extension_ft   # 60.5 - release_y
pitch_at_distance(traj, COMMIT_POINT_FT)   # where it was at the commit point
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-fit
#| eval: false
from smtstory.analytics.tunneling import fit_trajectory, at_distance, COMMIT_POINT_FT
traj = fit_trajectory(ball, t_pitch)
at_distance(traj, COMMIT_POINT_FT)
```

:::

## Radar Gun Live

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-radar
#| eval: false
source("../R/R06_pitching.R")
radar_gun(pitches, lineups, min_pitches = 30, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-radar
#| eval: false
from components import c06_pitching as c06
c06.radar_gun(tabs["pitches"], lu, top=10)
```

:::

| player | max | avg | pitches |
|---|---|---|---|
| KVN-7249 | 103.0 | 88.6 | 48 |
| ANI-1551 | 103.0 | **89.7** | 379 |
| VAS-0317 | 103.0 | 82.5 | 746 |

::: {.callout-note}
Readings above **103 mph** are filtered as single-frame tracking spikes — the
raw data contains a 193 mph artifact that would otherwise poison both the
leaderboard and every percentile built from it.
:::

![Pitch velocity distribution](../outputs/figures/fig_pitch_velo_dist.png)

## Velocity Heartbeat

Does a starter hold his gas? Per-pitch velocity with a rolling average, and the
difference between his first ten pitches and his last ten.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-heartbeat
#| eval: false
hb <- velocity_heartbeat(pitches, "y1_d122_IOL_VAS")
hb$summary
plot_velocity_heartbeat(hb)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-heartbeat
#| eval: false
data, summary = c06.velocity_heartbeat(tabs["pitches"], lu, "y1_d122_IOL_VAS")
summary
```

:::

## Effective Velocity

A pitcher who releases the ball a foot closer to the plate shortens the flight
and steals reaction time, so the ball **plays faster than the gun says**:

$$EV_{\text{eff}} = v \times \frac{60.5 - \text{ext}_{\text{league}}}{60.5 - \text{ext}_{\text{actual}}}$$

Extension is measured directly — in one sampled at-bat it ranged from 3.3 to
8.9 ft between pitchers, which is worth several perceived mph.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-effvelo
#| eval: false
effective_velocity_table(gs, plays, velos, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-effvelo
#| eval: false
c06.effective_velocity_table(game, plays, velos, top=10)
```

:::

## Late Life

::: {.callout-important}
## Gravity is not movement

Deviation from the straight line a hitter naively extrapolates has two causes,
and only one is interesting. **Gravity drops a 90 mph pitch about 39 inches** —
reporting that as "movement" makes every pitch look filthy and tells a fan
nothing.

Our first implementation did exactly that and produced 22–46 inch "breaks" on
every pitch in an at-bat. Subtracting the gravity component
($\tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$, with $t$ from velocity and release distance) leaves
**induced** vertical break — the aerodynamic part — which separates pitch types
cleanly:

| velo | extension | induced VB | horizontal | flight | shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 91.9 | 5.67 ft | **+19.3 in** | −13.6 in | 0.437 s | riding fastball |
| 77.7 | 6.82 ft | **+4.1 in** | −4.9 in | 0.507 s | breaking ball |
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-latelife
#| eval: false
late_break_in <- function(traj, velo_mph = NA_real_) {
  # ... straight-line baseline from the release direction ...
  t <- flight_time_s(ry, velo_mph)
  gravity_drop_in <- 0.5 * GRAVITY_FT_S2 * t^2 * 12
  induced_in <- raw_vert_in + gravity_drop_in   # remove gravity
  list(horizontal_in = horiz_in, induced_vertical_in = induced_in,
       gravity_drop_in = gravity_drop_in)
}

ll <- late_life_table(gs, plays, velos, top = 10)
plot_pitch_movement(ll)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-latelife
#| eval: false
c06.late_life_table(game, plays, velos, top=10)
```

:::

The movement plot — horizontal against induced vertical break — is the standard
"pitch shape" view, and it is what lets a scoreboard say *that was a different
pitch* and have the graphic prove it.
